summary: Fallback suppression prevented automatic fallback for pinned model during canary weight spike
description: Acme Retail reported a production traffic outage where requests pinned to a promoted model variant experienced prolonged delays and 504 timeouts during a canary weight shift. The router did not automatically route these requests to the configured fallback model due to a suppression heuristic in the fallback queue. This resulted in customer-facing timeouts and increased error rates for ~30 minutes before mitigation.
impact: All API calls for tenant acme-retail (dedicated) in us-west1 that depended on the pinned model fell back to 504 or >10s latencies. Estimated affected sessions: ~12k requests over 30m. Business impact: checkout flows degraded; several customers reported failed recommendations.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure tenant with a pinned model version (gptx-3.2b-fp16) and a canary rollout of the next variant with 10->40% weight ramp
2) Inject a sudden traffic spike from a real workload simulator (burst to 3x baseline RPS) while the canary-controller increments weight
3) Observe router decision logs and fallback queue behavior for pinned-session tokens
4) Note that requests that should have triggered fallback were suppressed for ~60s and then dropped with 504 responses
logs:
[router] 2026-03-14T15:22:11Z session=st_9a3f decision=pin_check PASS model=gptx-3.2b-fp16 -> route queued fallback_suppressed=true suppression_until=2026-03-14T15:23:10Z
[edge-proxy] 2026-03-14T15:22:55Z span=span_77a9 downstream=504 upstream=503 message=upstream_timeout
[canary-controller] 2026-03-14T15:23:05Z weight_adjust from=12 to=28 reason=auto-ramp
[serving-runtime] 2026-03-14T15:23:40Z gpu=pool-west-1 task_dropped reason=fallback-suppression-expired but backend-busy
comments: Maya Chen (Support): Customer reported spike at 15:22 PST; initial triage shows 504s from edge and increased router queue lengths.
Liam O'Connor (SRE): Reproducing locally with simulator; observed suppression flag on fallback queue. Opening with routing team.
Routing Team (internal): Confirmed suppression window configured to 60s to prevent oscillation. Under concurrency the suppression prevented enqueuing fallback attempts for pinned sessions.
Customer (Acme Retail): Confirmed mitigation lowered error rate after support applied temporary config change. Asking for root cause and permanent fix timeline.
investigation_notes: Fallback suppression was introduced to prevent rapid thrash during rolling promotions; it sets a suppression_until timestamp per session cohort.

During burst, many sessions set suppression_until and the canary weight increase caused more requests to hit capacity for the pinned variant, but suppression prevented fallback attempts while capacity remained constrained.
Router metrics show fallback_attempt_rate dropped by ~92% for the tenant between 15:22 and 15:24 while queue depth rose.
Serving runtime reported backend busy and started shedding requests once queue > 500; those requests then returned 504 at the edge.
Trace IDs: span_77a9, span_8b12, span_90d4 mapped to failing requests (linked in comment).
hypothesis: The suppression heuristic is too coarse-grained: it operates per-session-cohort without considering global capacity signals. When a canary weight shift and a traffic burst coincide, suppression prevents fallback for multiple cohorts simultaneously, creating a herd effect that blocks fallback routing until suppression expires.
workaround: Applied temporary mitigation at 15:42: reduced fallback suppression window from 60s -> 5s for acme-retail tenant and increased allowed concurrent fallback attempts to avoid herd suppression. Immediately observed error rate drop to baseline within 3 minutes.
resolution: Mitigation applied and customer confirmed restoration of normal traffic at 15:45. Next steps: (1) Routing team to patch suppression logic to include capacity and queue-depth signals (PR opened), (2) add per-tenant adaptive suppression thresholds, (3) add automated alert when fallback_attempt_rate drops >50% while queue depth >100 for >30s. Target for patch rollout: 2026-03-17. Postmortem to be filed after deployment.
